the expired page carries it. The Inngest wait timeout is the one writer of

The registry decides one record for each product ID. A filter passed
into it would make the reason of a hidden record decide the query, and the
two routes would then read the catalogue two ways.

⚠️ **An empty list is the correct answer for two different tenants.** A
caller that holds no `run.start` reads it, and so does a member of an
organization that installed nothing. Both mean the caller starts nothing,
and neither reply names a capability. Pass `available_only=false` to read

    registry: The reader of the product capabilities.

Raises:

      decorator answers 500. An empty catalogue for a full tenant would be
      the wrong answer.

handler: the resolver answers `connection_revoked` for it.

so the person can link the same LinkedIn login again: Unipile refuses a
second link of a login the application already holds. The removal is
best effort. A failure leaves the row revoked, and the log names the
error code and no account id. A repeat revoke removes again, so a person
recovers from a failed removal by revoking once more; an account that is
gone already answers a 404, which is logged and harmless. An account that

old row was revoked, and the new row is the one that owns the account.

post.description:
Writes one message and starts one turn.

The request never waits for a model call. The row commits before the `202`,
so a client that reloads at once reads its own message, and the answer
arrives on the conversation stream.

⚠️ **A repeated key answers `200` with the first message, and never
`409`.** It writes nothing and sends the turn again: the row committed
before the first send, so a send that raised would otherwise leave that
message unanswered for ever with no error to say so. Inngest drops the
second copy on the event id, so one turn runs.

⚠️ **The refusals are ordered `403`, then `400` and `413`, then `404`.**
The body and the header are checked before the conversation is read, so a
malformed request never tells a caller whether an id exists. Two `400`
answers come after the `404`: whether this conversation takes a draft, and
for which capability. Both need the row.

Args:
    conversation_id: The conversation the caller named.
    body: The text of the message, and the rows it is about.
    response: The response, so a repeated key answers `200`.
    idempotency_key: The delivery identity of this message.
    auth: The authenticated caller.
    service: The one writer of a message and its turn.
    conversations: The reader that proves the conversation is visible.

Returns:
    The stored message. It is the first message when a repeated key read it
    back, and never the text of the second request.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 403 for an impersonated session. 400 for a missing or
      oversized key, an empty text, a text over the bound, too many
      `entity_refs` and a malformed one. 413 for a draft over the bound.
      404 when this person owns no such conversation. 400 for a draft on
      an ordinary conversation, or for a capability the conversation does
      not name.

get.description:
Serves the live events of one conversation over SSE.

⚠️ **Subscribe, then send.** Redis Pub/Sub keeps no backlog, so an event
published before the client subscribed reaches nobody. The client opens
this stream before it posts a message, and it keeps it open for the life of
the conversation view.

⚠️ **This stream has no terminal event.** A run ends and a conversation
does not, so nothing closes it but its own bound. The client reconnects and
refetches `GET /messages`, which is why every outcome of a turn writes a
durable row.

Args:
    conversation_id: The conversation to follow.
    auth: The authenticated caller.
    streams: The reader of the conversation channel.

Returns:
    The event stream. A heartbeat keeps an idle connection open through a
    proxy, and the client reconnects on its own backoff.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 404, when this person owns no such conversation.

Lists the definitions this organization may see.

The page is a union: the caller's own rows in every state, plus the
platform templates that are `active`. A fork starts from a template, so a
list that hid them would leave `fork` unreachable.

Args:
    kind: agent, workflow or skill.
    origin: `platform` reads the templates alone, and `custom` reads this
      organization's own rows alone.
    state: draft, active or disabled. It narrows the organization's half;
      the template half stays `active` whatever this argument says.
    include_archived: Whether the page also holds the archived rows. The
      default hides them, because an archived definition is one the
      organization cleared from the Builder.
    cursor: The position a previous page returned.
    limit: How many definitions the page holds.
    auth: The authenticated caller.
    definitions: The reader of agent.definitions.

Returns:
    The page, and the cursor of the next one.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 400 for a cursor this endpoint did not write.

post.description:
Creates one draft.

It answers `201`, because it always mints a row. A create runs no
validation: a new draft is empty, and the first save reports what is
missing.

Args:
    body: The kind, the name and the starting configuration.
    auth: The authenticated caller.
    service: The one owner of the definition lifecycle.
    definitions: The reader of agent.definitions, for the links.

Returns:
    The new draft.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 403 when this actor may not change definitions here.

delete.description:
Removes one draft.

A published definition is disabled, never deleted: `runs_definition_fk`
restricts, and a run's audit trail must not be deletable from under it. So
an active or a disabled definition answers `409`.

It answers `204`. The row is gone, so there is nothing to read back.

Args:
    definition_id: The draft to remove.
    auth: The authenticated caller.
    service: The one owner of the definition lifecycle.

Returns:
    Nothing. The decorator owns the status, and it is the only writer of
    it: an endpoint that also built a `Response` would state 204 twice,
    and a change to one of the two would leave the other in place with no
    test failing.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 409 for a published definition, 403 for a non-admin, and
      404 when this organization owns no such definition.

get.description:
Reads one definition of this organization.

⚠️ **A platform template answers `404` here.** It carries no organization,
so the org-scoped read passes over it exactly as it passes over another
tenant's row. A template is visible through the list and through `fork`,
and the list row carries what an admin needs to choose one.

Args:
    definition_id: The definition to read.
    auth: The authenticated caller.
    definitions: The reader of agent.definitions.

Returns:
    The definition, with both configurations.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 404, when this organization owns no such definition.

post.description:
Hides one definition from the default list.

A published definition is never deleted. An active one is switched off
first, with the refusal `disable` gives when something still references
it. A draft or a disabled one takes the mark alone. A second press answers
`200` and writes nothing.

Args:
    definition_id: The definition to archive.
    auth: The authenticated caller.
    service: The one owner of the definition lifecycle.
    definitions: The reader of agent.definitions, for the links.

Returns:
    The definition as it now stands.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 409 when an active definition still references this one,
      403 for a non-admin or a managed row, and 404 when this organization
      owns no such definition.

Refuses new run trees of one definition.

⚠️ **It is not a stop button.** A workflow already running still starts its
child runs, including one that begins after a three day wait. An admin who
must stop one run cancels it.

It carries no token. An admin who presses it during an incident must not be
answered `stale` because a colleague saved a draft a second earlier.

A second press answers `200` and writes nothing.

Args:
    definition_id: The definition to switch off.
    auth: The authenticated caller.
    service: The one owner of the definition lifecycle.
    definitions: The reader of agent.definitions, for the links.

Returns:
    The definition as it now stands.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 409 when an active definition still references this one
      or the definition has never published, 403 for a non-admin, and 404
      when this organization owns no such definition.

patch.description:
Replaces the named fields of one draft.

The result carries a validation, and it is advisory: an invalid draft still
saves, because a draft is expected to be incomplete and the errors are what
tell the builder agent what is left.

`expected_updated_at` is an opaque string. This endpoint echoes it into the
statement and parses it nowhere.

Args:
    definition_id: The draft to write.
    body: The token and the fields to replace.
    auth: The authenticated caller.
    service: The one owner of the definition lifecycle.
    definitions: The reader of agent.definitions, for the links.

Returns:
    The saved draft, and what validation found.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 409 when the token no longer matches, 403 for a
      non-admin, and 404 when this organization owns no such definition.

post.description:
Returns one disabled definition to service.

It revalidates first. A definition this one references may have been
disabled while this one was off, so without the check an enable returns a
broken definition to service.

A second press answers `200` and writes nothing.

Args:
    definition_id: The definition to return to service.
    auth: The authenticated caller.
    service: The one owner of the definition lifecycle.
    definitions: The reader of agent.definitions, for the links.

Returns:
    The definition as it now stands.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 422 when the stored configuration can no longer
      validate, 409 when the definition has never published, 403 for a
      non-admin, and 404 when this organization owns no such definition.

Copies one template into this organization as a draft.

⚠️ **It is the one route that accepts a platform id**, because a fork is
how a template reaches an organization. The source must be `active`: a
draft holds no published configuration to copy, and a disabled row is
configuration an admin withdrew.

⚠️ **It carries no `Idempotency-Key`, so two calls mint two copies.** A
fork of a platform workflow is a deep fork: it copies the reachable set and
rewrites every id. The shared rule asks for a key on a route that starts a
run, and this route writes drafts. A draft cannot run and it deletes
cleanly, so a repeated fork leaves rows an admin removes.

Args:
    definition_id: The template to copy.
    auth: The authenticated caller.
    service: The one owner of the definition lifecycle.
    definitions: The reader of agent.definitions, for the links.

Returns:
    The new root draft.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 422 when the template names a definition that no longer
      resolves, 403 for a non-admin, and 404 when there is no active
      definition this caller may fork.

Makes the stored draft the runnable configuration.

A publish refused by a referrer answers `422` naming it, and writes
nothing: the service validates everything before it writes one byte.

Args:
    definition_id: The definition to publish.
    body: The token the caller read.
    auth: The authenticated caller.
    service: The one owner of the definition lifecycle.
    definitions: The reader of agent.definitions, for the links.

Returns:
    The published definition.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 422 for an invalid configuration or a referrer this
      publish would break, 409 for a stale token or the referrer cap, 403
      for a non-admin, and 404 when this organization owns no such
      definition.

Returns one definition to the default list.

It clears the mark and nothing else. A published definition stays
disabled, so `enable` remains a separate step.

Args:
    definition_id: The definition to unarchive.
    auth: The authenticated caller.
    service: The one owner of the definition lifecycle.
    definitions: The reader of agent.definitions, for the links.

Returns:
    The definition as it now stands.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 403 for a non-admin, and 404 when this organization
      owns no such definition.

Validates one draft and writes nothing.

It never answers `422`. That status is a refusal of a write, and this route
makes none: the caller reads `validation.ok`. It runs no authority check
either, for the same reason.

Args:
    definition_id: The draft to validate.
    auth: The authenticated caller.
    service: The one owner of the definition lifecycle.
    definitions: The reader of agent.definitions, for the links.

Returns:
    The definition, and what validation found.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 404, when this organization owns no such definition.

get.description:
Lists what this organization may spend.

An organization that set no ceiling answers an empty page, and never a
`404`. The organization is there, and it has no cap.

Args:
    auth: The authenticated caller.
    ceilings: The reader of agent.cost_ceilings.

Returns:
    Every ceiling of this organization, ordered by kind.

put.description:
Sets one ceiling, or removes it.

⚠️ **A null `value_cents` removes the row, and it is the one path back to
no cap.** The column takes zero, and zero stops every run, because the
accrual check compares `spent >= cap`. An admin who could only write a
number could never undo a ceiling.

It carries no write token. One scalar has nothing to merge, so two
administrators racing on the day cap leave the later value.

Args:
    body: The kind, and the value or null.
    auth: The authenticated caller.
    authority: The reader of the live rights.
    ceilings: The writer of agent.cost_ceilings.

Returns:
    The ceiling this organization now holds. `value_cents` is null after a
    removal.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 403 when this actor may not write here.

get.description:
Lists the count budgets of the caller's own accounts, or every account.

A member reads the budgets of their own connections. An organization admin
reads every live connection of the organization. Each line names the
platform default, the override, the cap in force now and the effects held
in the current window. A caller with no connection reads an empty page.

Args:
    auth: The authenticated caller.
    authority: The reader of the live rights.
    connections: The reader of agent.connections.
    budgets: The reader of the overrides and the ledger.

Returns:
    One entry for each live connection the caller may see.

put.description:
Lowers one count budget, or removes the override.

⚠️ **A value above the platform default answers `422`.** An admin can
lower a budget and never raise it. The platform default is set below the
limits an outside service enforces, so a higher value would only move an
account closer to a restriction.

Args:
    body: The connection, the class, the window, and the value or null.
    auth: The authenticated caller.
    authority: The reader of the live rights.
    connections: The reader of agent.connections.
    budgets: The writer of the overrides.

Returns:
    The line as it now reads.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 403 for a member, 404 for a connection this
      organization does not hold, and 422 for a class or window the
      provider does not limit or a value above the default.

get.description:
Lists the proposed actions, oldest first by default, one page at a time.

The Handled view reads in one call: its statuses, `since` and the
`newest_decided` sort. Its Approved group passes `approved` and
`sending`; no status adds another.

Args:
    status: Only the actions in these statuses; repeat the parameter for
      more. The default is the queue, `pending_approval`.
    campaign_id: Only the actions of this campaign, or every campaign.
    type: Only the actions of this type, or every type.
    since: Only the actions decided at or after this time: approved,
      rejected, executed, or failed.
    sort: `oldest` by created_at, or `newest_decided`, the newest
      decision first. `newest_decided` needs a `since` of the last 31
      days, else 422.
    limit: How many actions the page holds.
    offset: How many actions to skip before the page.
    auth: The authenticated caller.
    review: The Review queue reads.

Returns:
    The page, the count of every matching action, and `has_more`. The
    queue, `pending_approval`, also answers `due_soon`: the count of the
    enrollments that come due in the next 24 hours. Another status set
    answers null.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 422 when `newest_decided` has no recent `since`.

Reads one proposed action, the same item as the list.

Args:
    action_id: The action. Another organization's action answers 404.
    auth: The authenticated caller.
    review: The Review queue reads.

Returns:
    The action.

post.description:
Approves one proposed action: the text, `to` and the hash freeze.

A retry with the same payload answers 200 and sends the same event.

Args:
    action_id: The action. Another organization's action answers 404.
    body: The edited text fields, or none to approve the draft.
    auth: The authenticated caller.
    review: The Review queue.

Returns:
    The action as it now reads.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 422 when the edit fails the draft check.

Rejects one proposed action, then regenerates, stops, skips or switches.

A retry with the same `then` answers 200 and repeats the side effect.
`remember` with a `then` other than `regenerate` answers 422. A
`switch_channel` that the campaign or the person does not allow answers
409 `channel_unavailable`. A switch to email also needs an address that
is not suppressed. A switch to LinkedIn also needs a sender with
a live LinkedIn connection, and a person who is not declined or
suppressed on LinkedIn.

Args:
    action_id: The action. Another organization's action answers 404.
    body: What follows, and the reason.
    auth: The authenticated caller.
    review: The Review queue.

Returns:
    The action as it now reads.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 422 for a reason that holds an unpaired surrogate.

get.description:
Lists the campaigns, newest first, one page at a time.

Each campaign holds the count of its enrollments per status and its
outcome counts.

Args:
    status: Only the campaigns in this status, or every status.

Returns:
    The page in `items`, the count of every matching campaign, and

Creates a `paused` campaign. The caller owns it, and its mailbox sends.

`strategy_id` names the strategy. A missing one answers 422

Args:

Returns:
    The new campaign.

Reads the Outreach totals of the organization, for the summary strip.

Returns:

Reads one campaign with its counts and its remembered feedback.

Args:

patch.description:
Writes the given campaign fields. An archived campaign answers 409.

A new `strategy_id` must name a live strategy, and the campaign goal

A follow-up bound past the stored other bound answers 422. The sender
is not a field: it stays the creator.

Args:

Returns:

get.description:
Reads one page of the sends, replies and decisions, newest first.

A malformed cursor answers 422 with the code `invalid_cursor`.

Args:
    campaign_id: The campaign.

    limit: The most items of the page.
    cursor: The `next_cursor` of the previous page.

    The page and the cursor of the next page, or None on the last page.

The rows that wait on a review come first, then the next step:

Each row names the person, the email, the title, the company and the

    campaign_id: The campaign.

    limit: How many enrollments the page holds.
    offset: How many enrollments to skip before the page.

    auth: The authenticated caller.
    campaigns: The campaign service.

Returns:
    The page, the count of every matching enrollment, and `has_more`.

get.description:
Lists the rules of this organization.

The page holds the disabled rules too. `enabled` is how an admin turns the
kill switch off rather than deleting it, and an admin edits a rule they
turned off.

⚠️ **There is no detail route, so each row carries `updated_at`.** It is
the write token, and a client that could not read it could not `PATCH`.

`action` matches the column by equality. It is an admin filter, and never
the engine match: which rules govern one action is the checkpoint's
question.

Args:
    action: One action, or None for every action.
    cursor: The position a previous page returned.
    limit: How many rules the page holds.
    auth: The authenticated caller.
    policies: The reader of agent.policies.

Returns:
    The page, and the cursor of the next one.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 400 for a cursor this endpoint did not write.

post.description:
Writes one rule.

The organization comes from the token, and never from the body.

Args:
    body: Every column the caller may set.
    auth: The authenticated caller.
    authority: The reader of the live rights.
    policies: The writer of agent.policies.
    catalogue: Every action a rule may bind to.

Returns:
    The new rule.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 400 for a rule this deploy cannot govern, 403 for a
      non-admin, 404 for a definition this organization does not own, and
      409 for a duplicate name or the rule past the read bound.

delete.description:
Removes one rule.

It carries no write token. A delete is an intentional act, and a rule an
admin removed under another admin's edit is still removed.

Args:
    policy_id: The rule to remove.
    auth: The authenticated caller.
    authority: The reader of the live rights.
    policies: The writer of agent.policies.

Returns:
    Nothing. The decorator owns the status, and it is the only writer of
    it.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 403 for a non-admin, and 404 when this organization owns
      no such rule.

patch.description:
Replaces the named columns of one rule.

⚠️ **The save check reads the merged rule, and never the patch alone.** A
rule reading `recipient_is_new` moved onto an action that declares nothing
would otherwise save, and then deny every call of that action.

`expected_updated_at` is an opaque string. This endpoint echoes it into the
statement and parses it nowhere.

Args:
    policy_id: The rule to write.
    body: The token, and the columns to replace.
    auth: The authenticated caller.
    authority: The reader of the live rights.
    policies: The writer of agent.policies.
    catalogue: Every action a rule may bind to.

Returns:
    The saved rule.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 400 for an empty patch or a rule this deploy cannot
      govern, 403 for a non-admin, 404 when this organization owns no such
      rule, and 409 for a stale token, a duplicate name or the rule past
      the read bound.

get.description:
Lists the prospects of this organization in the sort the caller names.

A caller that names no review state reads every one of them. A Run
returns prospects and a reviewer then moves some of them, so a default
state would hide those rows from the page that reads that Run.

The three sorts are `score`, `signal_strength` and `discovered`.
`discovered` is the default, and it reads `first_seen_at`, which is the
date this organization first saw the company. `score` reads
`opportunity_score` and `signal_strength` reads `latest_signal_score`.
Both put an ungraded row last.

`ids` names the prospects to read, at most one page of them. A finished
Run names its prospects in its result, and a later Run can move a
prospect's `last_seen_run_id`. The page that reads the Run therefore
reads its prospects by id, with one request and not one request each.

Three filters narrow the read. `people_state` names one people state.
`signal_type` keeps a prospect when one attached signal has the type, not
only the strongest signal the row names. `search` matches the company,
the person or the employer on a name or a domain. A cursor stays valid
only under the filters that wrote it.

`saved_search_id` keeps the prospects one saved search returned.
`min_score` and `max_score` keep an inclusive band of `opportunity_score`,
and a bound drops an ungraded row. A floor above the ceiling answers `422`.

⚠️ **A cursor belongs to one sort.** The three sorts order the same rows
three ways, so a position under one names a different row under another. A
cursor from another sort answers `400`, and the caller reads the first
page of the new sort instead.

post.description:
Writes one curation intent to many prospects.

The intent is `watch`, `dismiss` or `restore`, as the single routes write.
The answer is `200` and sorts each prospect into one outcome list. A
promoted, missing or foreign prospect is an outcome, not a refusal, so
one such prospect does not stop the others.

Promotes many prospects into CRM, one after the other.

Each item promotes as the single promote route does. A refused prospect
is a `failed` result with the reason, and the next prospect still
promotes. The answer holds one result for each item, in request order.

get.description:
Reads the first prospect page of each saved search in one request.

The Launchpad groups its leads by saved search. One request for the
whole set replaces one request for each search. Each group applies the
filters and the sort of the list route, and holds no cursor. A
repeated id reads once, and the groups keep the order the caller named.
At most `_GROUP_CONCURRENCY` group reads run at one time.

⚠️ **This route is declared before `/{prospect_id}`**, for the reason
`/counts` gives.

Counts the prospects of this organization in each review state.

The inbox names a number on each tab. Every state answers a number, and a
state that holds no prospect answers 0. Each number is exact, not capped.

⚠️ **This route is declared before `/{prospect_id}`.** FastAPI matches in
declaration order. The other order reads `counts` as a prospect id and
answers 422.

and a type with no prospect is not in the list.

⚠️ **This route is declared before `/{prospect_id}`**, for the reason

Deletes one prospect with its people, its signals and its search links.

Only a platform superadmin can delete, to debug a run. A member of the
organization uses `dismiss`, which keeps a company out of later runs.

The delete accepts every review state and changes no CRM row. It keeps no
record of the company, so a later Run that finds the same company writes a
new prospect at `new`.

The panel shows one button, and this route is what the button runs. Each

task, `promote` runs the promotion service the promote route runs, and
`watch` and `dismiss` run the curation the two curation routes run.

**`create_task` promotes the prospect first when it holds no CRM company.**
A task hangs on a CRM company, so a prospect that never entered the CRM
gains one here. It promotes the person the action names, or the best
matched attached person when the action names none.

A prospect that carries no suggested action answers `409`. There is no
move to perform, and a default move would act on a guess. Every refusal
the underlying action raises travels unchanged.
Moves one non-promoted prospect to dismissed.

Adds one person a reader names to a company prospect.

is written to global Intelligence, and the name fills only an empty field.
The typed title and email stay on the prospect row, and each fills only a
value the profile does not have. A person with no profile stays on the
prospect row. The prospect then holds people, and its people state is
`found`.

Starts one People Search Run for the company of a prospect.

The Run looks for the persona in the body, or for the people the
description names. An empty body looks for the decision makers of the
company. The prospect holds the Run until it
ends, and the platform then attaches the people it found. A second start
while the Run is live answers `409`. Two starts with one persona in one
minute answer one Run.

patch.description:
Corrects one person a company prospect lists.

`person_id` is the prospect person row. A field the body leaves out keeps
its value, and a null title or email clears the typed value. A typed title
and email stay on the prospect row and are shown over the profile value. A
new LinkedIn URL moves the row to the global person of that profile. A
person in the CRM is written there too. A promoted prospect takes the
edit. A person prospect, a row that changed after `expected_updated_at`,
a profile or a name the prospect already lists, and an email or a LinkedIn
URL another CRM person holds each answer `409`.

post.description: Promotes one prospect and its selected people into CRM.

Returns one watched or dismissed prospect to new.

This route undoes `watch` and `dismiss`. The panel shows it as Unwatch on
a watched prospect and as Restore on a dismissed one, and both send this
one request.

A prospect already at `new` answers `200` and writes nothing. A promoted
prospect answers `409`: promotion wrote CRM rows, and a review state does
not take them back.

get.description: Lists the bounded signals attached to one visible prospect.

post.description:
Records that a person closed the suggested action card.

The panel shows the card again on every read while the stamp is null.
This route writes the stamp, so the card stays closed.

The stamp does not change the review state and does not clear
`suggested_action`, so the act route still performs the move. A repeat
call keeps the first stamp and answers `200`.

**The dismissal belongs to one recommendation, not to the prospect.** A
Run that writes a different `suggested_action` clears the stamp, so a new
recommendation shows a new card. A Run that repeats the same move keeps
the card closed.
Moves one non-promoted prospect to watching.

get.description:
Lists the runs of one organization.

It returns the top of each tree by default. `root_only=false` returns the
children too, and `parent_run_id=` alone returns the children of one run,
which is how a caller reads the children a detail does not carry.

`root_only` is unset by default rather than true, so naming a parent is
enough. A caller that reads `child_count` on a detail and then asks for
`?parent_run_id=<id>` gets the children, and it does not have to know that
a second parameter contradicts the default it never set.

Args:
    root_only: True returns root runs alone. Unset means true when no
      parent is named, and false when one is.
    parent_run_id: Returns the children of one run.
    definition_id: Returns the runs of one definition.
    capability_id: Returns the runs of these capabilities. Repeat the
      parameter to name more than one. A product page holds this value and
      holds no definition ID, so it is the selector a product list uses.
      The Signals history names `signals.search` and `people.signals`. A
      rename moves `definition_name` and never this.
    status: Returns the runs in one status.
    source: Returns the runs one kind of entry point started. The Sonar
      sidebar lists the `trigger` runs, which a schedule started.
    saved_search_id: Returns the runs one saved search started, from
      Run now or from its schedule. The saved search detail page links to
      this list.
    cursor: The position a previous page returned.
    limit: How many runs the page holds.
    include_result: True puts the frozen result of each Run on its row.
      The Companies page shows the results of many Runs, and this lets it
      send one request and not one detail read per Run. The default is
      false, so a list reads no payload column.
    auth: The authenticated caller.
    runs: The reader of agent.runs.
    searches: The reader of the saved searches. It names each Run that
      a saved search started.

Returns:
    The page, and the cursor of the next one.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 400 for a cursor this endpoint did not write, and for
      `root_only=true` with a `parent_run_id`. A root has no parent, so the
      pair names the empty set, and a caller that meant one of the two
      would read no run and see no error.

post.description:
Starts one run.

The endpoint builds the same StartRunCommand the front door and the
triggers build, and it maps the closed answer. It adds no status of its
own, and it writes no run state.

⚠️ **The key is namespaced per caller.** RunManager hashes
`(source, key)`, and the source is `api` for every HTTP start, so an
unchanged header would let two people in one organization who reuse a key
read each other's run. The stored key is unique per organization, and two
people share one organization.

There is no 409 on a repeated start. The start key lives on the run row, so
a duplicate always reads a committed run and answers 200 with `outcome`.

Args:
    body: The definition and the input.
    idempotency_key: The delivery identity of this start.
    auth: The authenticated caller.
    manager: The one owner of the run lifecycle.
    runs: The reader of agent.runs.
    usage: The meter that sums the tree.

Returns:
    The run detail, carrying the outcome.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 400 for a missing or over-long key. 422 for input that
      the capability contract of the definition refuses. The status of
      the refusal, for every other outcome.

post.description:
Stops one run and its descendants.

Cancel is idempotent by construction: the second call matches zero rows.
Cancelling a finished run is still a success, and the answer carries the
run detail, so the caller reads the status it produced rather than the
status it asked for.

The visibility read runs first. `RunManager.cancel()` answers nothing and
returns quietly for a run this organization does not own, so without that
read a foreign run id would answer 200 with no run.

Args:
    run_id: The run the caller named.
    auth: The authenticated caller.
    manager: The one owner of the run lifecycle.
    runs: The reader of agent.runs.
    usage: The meter that sums the tree.
    searches: The reader of the saved searches.

Returns:

Raises:

get.description:
Lists the durable partial rows of one live or finished run.

⚠️ **This is the durable half of the reconnect contract.** `GET
/{run_id}/stream` keeps no backlog, so a client that just subscribed reads
this page next, then applies whatever it buffered meanwhile. See
`stream_run` and `interfaces/surfaces.md`, Reconnect.

Each row carries the same `result_id`, `ref` and `display` the live
`result.item_ready` event of the same row carried, ordered the same way
the search found them. A capability with no durable row answers an empty
page: its page reads its results from the durable result endpoint
instead, exactly as `_PUBLIC_ITEM_KINDS` in `stream.py` decides for the
live channel.

Args:
    run_id: The run whose rows to read. A child carries no capability of
      its own, so this resolves the capability of its root, exactly as
      the live stream does, and reads the hit store keyed on that root.
    cursor: The position a previous page returned.
    limit: How many rows the page holds.
    auth: The authenticated caller.
    runs: The reader of agent.runs.
    items: The reader of the hit store of each capability.

Returns:
    The page, and the cursor of the next one.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 404, when this organization owns no such run. 400 for
      a cursor this endpoint did not write. 422 for a limit outside
      `_PAGE_MIN`..`_PAGE_MAX`.

Read product milestones across a root run and its children.

Child IDs are refused instead of silently returning a different run tree.
Unknown capabilities answer an empty stage list with the actual run state.

Lists the spans of one run.

It resolves the run first, so a principal from another organization
receives 404 on the spans of a run it cannot see and the span read never
runs. A malformed `since` or `cursor` answers `400` before that read, as a
bad cursor already did: neither refusal names the run.

⚠️ **`scope` keys the read, and `run` is the default.** Both columns are
indexed, so the wrong one answers a whole tree instead of one run. `run`
keeps the old answer, and a caller opens a child tree by asking for that
child. `scope=tree` keys on `root_run_id` and answers every span below the
root in one page sequence.

A node that runs an agent starts a child Run, and that child's spans carry
its own run id. ENG-2559 measured a company.search Run whose page answered
two spans while the tree held five: the planner's `run`, `segment` and
`llm` spans were under the child. Ask with `scope=tree` to see where a Run
spent its time.

⚠️ **`tree` answers the tree of the root, whichever member is named.** A
child carries the root's id in `root_run_id` and never its own, so the
read resolves the root from the run it already read. Naming a child and
naming its root therefore answer the same page. That is not a widening of
access: every run of one tree belongs to one organization, and the caller
could already read the root directly.

⚠️ **`since=` filters `updated_at`, and it never filters `started_at`.** A
tool span that opened before a gap and closed inside it keeps its older
`started_at`, so a filter on that column never reports the close and the
client draws the span as running for the life of the page.

⚠️ **`since=` also changes the order of the page**, onto the index the
reconnect reads. One route therefore holds two orders, so the cursor names
the one it was written for and a mismatched pair answers `400`. Untagged, a
cursor from a `since=` page replayed without `since=` would page
`started_at` from an `updated_at` value and answer quietly.

Args:
    run_id: The run whose spans to read. With `scope=tree` any member of
      a tree names that whole tree.
    scope: `run` for the spans this run wrote, `tree` for every span below
      its root.
    since: Read the spans that moved at or after this instant. It carries
      a time zone, and a naive value is refused.

      ⚠️ A reconnecting client sends the newest `updated_at` it holds, and
      it follows `next_cursor` to exhaustion before it moves this value.
      The filter is inclusive, and the orphan closer stamps every span of
      one statement identically, so a client that only ever re-sends its
      newest value re-reads that whole group and never reaches the span
      after it.
    cursor: The position a previous page returned.
    limit: How many spans the page holds.
    auth: The authenticated caller.
    runs: The reader of agent.runs.
    spans: The reader of agent.spans.

Returns:
    The page, and the cursor of the next one.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 404, when this organization owns no such run. 400 for a
      cursor this endpoint did not write, one written for the other order,
      or a `since` with no time zone.
Read one span's stored payload after checking ownership of its run.

Serves the live events of one run over SSE.

⚠️ **It reads the channel of `run_id`, and it resolves no root.** The
publisher mirrors a child event to the root channel, so a root
subscription already follows the whole tree. A reader that rewrote the id
would make every child channel unreachable.

⚠️ **A live event is a hint, and the durable record is the answer.** The
stream keeps no backlog, so a reconnecting client subscribes first, then
reads the run and `GET /runs/{id}/spans?since=`, then applies what it
buffered. See `interfaces/surfaces.md`, Reconnect.

The stream closes on a terminal event of this run, at a bounded lifetime,
or when the caller goes away. A run that already ended closes at once.

Args:
    run_id: The run to follow.
    auth: The authenticated caller.
    streams: The reader of the run channel.

Returns:
    The event stream. A heartbeat keeps an idle connection open through a
    proxy, and the client reconnects on its own backoff.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 404, when this organization owns no such run.

patch.description:

⚠️ **The save check reads the merged row, and never the patch alone.** A
patch that nulls `cron` on a schedule row, or moves the zone under an
expression it was never proved against, would otherwise save and then stop
firing.

⚠️ **`authored_by` is not repointed.** An admin who edits another admin's
row edits it; they do not take it over. Repointing it silently would widen
or narrow every future mint of that row.

`expected_updated_at` is an opaque string. This endpoint echoes it into the
statement and parses it nowhere.

Args:

    body: The token, and the columns to replace.
    auth: The authenticated caller.
    authority: The reader of the live rights.
    rights: The same reader, for the authored scopes.
    triggers: The writer of agent.triggers.
    builders: Every input builder this deploy registers.

    The saved trigger.

Raises:

      row, 409 for a stale token or a duplicate name, and 422 for a row
      that could never fire or a write that moves a saved-search row.

operation is immune to the per-request-timeout fan-out that used to
leave a random partial result on prod. Large id lists are split into

the CRM People table when hydrating off-page linked companies for hover

can merge into the same store; unknown / soft-deleted / cross-org ids are
silently dropped.

get.description:
SSE stream of real-time notification events for the caller.

Clients consume this endpoint to replace the 30s ``/unread-count``
poll. The service publishes ``insert`` / ``update`` / ``update_all``
events to a per-user Redis channel after every DB write; this
endpoint subscribes and forwards each message as an SSE ``data:``
frame. On client disconnect or 30-minute timeout, the stream closes
cleanly and the client reconnects with `Last-Event-ID` semantics
handled by the shared SSE client.

The database is never touched directly by the frontend — Redis
pub/sub is the DB-agnostic transport, so the storage layer remains
swappable (ENG-769).

A single process-wide ``NotificationFanout`` holds one Redis pub/sub
connection and dispatches to per-stream queues, so connection use is
O(1) in concurrent viewers rather than one connection per stream.
Return the caller's current unread notification count.

Return the effective user's identity.

When a superadmin sends ``X-Act-As-User``, ``user_id`` and
``organization_id`` reflect the impersonated target, and
``impersonator_id`` is set to the caller. ``claims`` always carry
the caller's JWT (the impersonator's), so the client can tell who
is actually authenticated. This is what lets CLI helpers that
bootstrap an ``organization_id`` from ``/whoami`` correctly target
the impersonated org instead of the caller's own.
